Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including:

- TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)

- Fortune Change the World (2024)

- CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)

- Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)

- Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)

- Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)

- Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role

Maven is looking for a VP of Business Operations to own the operating engine behind our core business — beginning with one of the most important numbers in the company: enrollments. This role is accountable for driving member enrollment into Maven’s programs across our core business and, by extension, the revenue those enrollments generate. It also owns three central functions that determine how well the rest of the company executes: AI enablement, central operations, and strategy & operations.

Enrollment is not a single-team problem. It sits at the intersection of nearly every function at Maven, and this role is built for someone who thrives there. You’ll partner daily with Client Success (who own the client relationships that unlock eligible populations), Marketing (member acquisition and lifecycle), Product (enrollment experience and funnel), Finance (targets, forecasting, and unit economics), Data (measurement, segmentation, and attribution), and Clinical and Operations teams. Because so many teams touch enrollment, a core part of the job is holding those cross-functional partners accountable to their piece of the machine — the engine only works when every team delivers its part.

This is a senior leadership role with a broad and growing remit. You will build, lead, and develop a multi-function organization — including leaders who own member growth, central operations, strategy & ops, and AI enablement — and you will be measured on what those teams collectively deliver. You set the strategy, define the operating cadence, and raise the bar for analytical rigor across a wide cross-functional surface.

We’re also looking for someone who can expand the definition of the job. A great deal of enrollment optimization work is already underway, but there is not enough strategic thinking about fundamentally new ways to drive enrollments — approaches that don’t simply depend on securing permission to communicate with a client’s employees. You are accountable for ensuring your team finds and opens those new avenues, and for creating the conditions and analytical foundation that let them do it.

What You’ll Do

- Own member growth for the Core Business: Be directly accountable for enrollment targets across Maven’s core business and for the revenue those enrollments drive. Set the strategy, build the plan, and act as a control tower across all cross-functional teams driving revenue to deliver the results quarter over quarter.

- Build and run a scalable enrollment engine: Own the full journey from eligible population to enrolled, activated member — spanning client launches, member acquisition and messaging, the enrollment product experience, and re-engagement of eligible-but-not-enrolled members.

- Deliver AI enablement across the organization: Own the function that introduces new ways of working with AI at Maven — and, just as importantly, measures them. Build the adoption playbook, instrument usage and impact team by team, and continuously optimize the value the company gets from how Mavens use AI in their day-to-day work.

- Lead the central operations team: Own the function that enables our member operations and client operations teams to deliver more operationally excellent service. Ensure the systems, tooling, and processes both teams rely on are effective and scalable — built to absorb growth rather than constrain it.

- Lead the strategy and operations team: Own a central strategy & ops function that brings analytical rigor and operating discipline to teams across the org, with specific focus on partnering with Sales, Client Success, and Payer Growth.

- Optimize relentlessly around data: Build and consistently iterate on the funnel, and create systems that enable quick diagnoses of opportunities. Build operational metrics that act as leading KPIs for each team contributing to enrollments and bring quantitative rigor into how teams execute against targets.

- Hold the cross-functional machine accountable: Partner daily with Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Payer, Sales, and Operations — and hold each team accountable to its operational KPIs in the enrollment process. Serve as the connective tissue that keeps every part of the engine delivering.

- Instrument and forecast: Partner with Data and Finance to build the measurement, segmentation, attribution, and forecasting needed to know exactly what is and isn’t working, and to forecast enrollment and revenue with confidence.

What You’ll Bring

- 12+ years of experience driving growth, enrollment, acquisition, revenue, or business operations outcomes, with a track record of personally owning and hitting a number — ideally in healthcare, benefits, marketplaces, consumer subscription, or another environment with a complex funnel and multiple stakeholders.

- Proven people and organizational leadership. You have built and led multi-team or multi-function organizations, hired and developed leaders beneath you, and delivered results through a team rather than solely through your own execution.

- Elite quantitative ability as a core competency. You can build and interrogate a funnel model yourself, size opportunities, design experiments, and instinctively optimize around data rather than intuition. Strong quant is non-negotiable.

- Strategic range across functions. You can set direction for several distinct teams at once — growth, operations, strategy, and enablement — sequence their priorities, and push each toward fundamentally new approaches rather than incremental improvement.

- Operational systems and scaling experience. You have owned the tooling, processes, and systems that service or operations teams depend on, and know how to make them effective and scalable ahead of demand.

- AI fluency and conviction. You have a point of view on where AI creates real leverage in a business, and the discipline to measure it rather than assume it.

- Cross-functional leadership and accountability. Proven ability to align and mobilize many teams — Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Operations — around a shared goal without direct authority over most of them, and to hold each accountable to its operational commitments.

- Commercial instincts. You understand how enrollment translates into revenue and unit economics, and you can partner with Finance on targets and forecasting.

- Comfort in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment with high visibility and direct accountability for a top-line company metric.

The base salary range for this role is $275,000 - $320,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive bonus, equity, and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on qualifications, experience, and skillset.

Maven embraces a flexible hybrid work model. Our teams primarily operate from the New York Metropolitan area, NY, and remotely via San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, Seattle, WA. For those in our New York City office, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to work onsite three days a week  (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). For those based in Boston, DC, Chicago, Seattle, and San Francisco, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to attend monthly Work Together Days within these cities. About the Role:

Maven is looking for a Director of Marketing Operations who will own the systems, data, and reporting infrastructure behind our B2B Growth Marketing team — from HubSpot/Salesforce instrumentation to pipeline attribution to the budget that funds it all. This person will lead a team across marketing analytics, marketing operations, and web optimization, and serve as the go-to partner for Sales, RevOps, Strategic Finance, and Client Success on shared data and reporting. Reporting to the Senior Director of Growth, they'll bring structure and rigor to a fast-moving org, ensuring marketing's numbers hold up in front of executive leadership.

What You’ll Do:

Marketing Technology, Data & Attribution

- HubSpot instrumentation (and its integration with Salesforce): own lead management strategy, campaign orchestration and tracking, and stage definitions for the B2B funnel.

- Pipeline attribution: own marketing's multi-touch attribution methodology and represent it in cross-team pipeline conversations.

- Data governance: maintain data dictionaries and definitions (MQL/MQA thresholds, pipeline vs. bookings vs. revenue) so reporting stays consistent as tools and AI use expand.

- Martech stack: own B2B-facing tools and integrations, including CaliberMind, GA4, HubSpot, Qualified, Webflow, and evaluate new tooling as needs evolve.

- Training and enablement: ensure the has the resources and knowledge to own the reporting and orchestration of their channels.

Analytics & Reporting

- KPI ownership: define and maintain B2B marketing metrics (MQLs, MQAs, pipeline coverage, Pipe-Spend ratio) and the reporting cadence behind them.

- Executive reporting: build and deliver pipeline briefings and performance readouts for B2B marketing leadership.

- Dashboards: own the B2B analytics stack across CaliberMind, Looker, Data Studio, Salesforce, and GA4, and keep it accurate as definitions change.

- FY planning support: partner with Strategic Finance and RevOps on fiscal year target-setting, run-rate projections, and scenario modeling for B2B pipeline and budget as well as org-level OKR setting.

Budget & Planning

- Budget ownership: oversee the B2B marketing budget, including forecast, actuals, monthly reconciliation, and shifts across programs and months.

- Vendor management: track spend and manage relationships with external vendors.

About the Role:

We're looking for a GRC Manager to own governance, risk, and compliance for our B2B health benefits platform. You'll act as the team lead for our GRC function, working closely with one other team member to run audits, write policies, answer RFIs, and monitor controls day to day.

This role touches almost every team: partnering with Engineering, IT, and HR to gather evidence and close gaps; working directly with customers and their security teams during due diligence; and managing auditor relationships through certification cycles. You'll also bring solid project management skills, sequencing audits, tracking remediation, and hitting deadlines across multiple concurrent workstreams. You'll report directly to the CISO/Head of Security and act as the organization's primary voice on compliance posture. You will interface internally and externally with customers, auditors, and partners.

Our platform facilitates virtual health visits for employer-sponsored benefits, which means security, privacy, and compliance are core to customer trust and our ability to sell into enterprise and health-plan accounts.

What You'll Do:

External Audit & Certification Management

- Own continuation and renewal of our SOC 2 (Type II) and HITRUST certifications end-to-end. You'll scope each cycle, pull evidence, work directly with auditors, and track remediation through to the final report.

- Lead the ground-up establishment of ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification programs. That means gap assessments, control mapping, writing ISMS/AIMS policies and statements of applicability, gaining cross team buy in, and getting us ready for initial certification audits.

- Manage the annual/ongoing audit calendar across all frameworks, coordinating with internal stakeholders (Engineering, IT, HR, Legal) to gather evidence and close findings on time.

- Track regulatory and framework changes (HIPAA, state privacy laws, ISO updates) and translate them into control updates.

Customer-Facing Security & Compliance

- Serve as the primary owner of security questionnaires and RFIs/RFPs for the Sales and Customer Success teams. Ensure responses to prospect and customer’s due-diligence requests are accurate and on deadline.

- Maintain a security knowledge base / answer library to reduce turnaround time on recurring questions.

- Partner with Sales Engineering and Account teams to represent our security and compliance posture directly in customer calls when needed. You'll join customer calls directly when security is a blocker in the deal.

- Manage relationships with customers' internal security/compliance teams during onboarding and renewal cycles.

Internal Audit & Control Monitoring

- Build and run an internal audit/control-monitoring program focused first on verifying that externally audited controls are actually operating day-to-day.

- Flag control gaps or process drift to the CISO/Head of Security before they become audit findings.

- Over time, expand scope beyond audited-control verification into broader internal audit territory (policy adherence, vendor risk, operational risk) as bandwidth allows.

Required:

- 6+ years of experience in GRC, information security compliance, or IT audit, with direct ownership of at least one SOC 2 or similar audit cycle from start to finish.

- Working knowledge of SOC 2, HITRUST, and ISO 27001 frameworks hands-on .

- Experience responding to customer security questionnaires/RFIs, ideally in a B2B SaaS or healthcare-adjacent environment.

- Strong cross-team collaboration skills. You'll regularly work with Engineering, IT, HR, Legal, and Sales to gather evidence, close control gaps, and keep everyone aligned on deadlines.

- Solid project management instincts: able to sequence overlapping audits and certification projects, track dependencies and remediation items, and hit dates without needing someone else to manage the plan for you.

- Strong written communication; you'll be writing policies, RFI responses, and audit narratives that both auditors and non-technical stakeholders need to understand.

- Direct experience standing up a new certification (SOC2, HITRUST, ISO 27001 and/or the newer 42001 AI management standard) rather than just maintaining an existing one.

- Experience partnering with Sales/Sales Engineering as a technical or compliance resource during the deal cycle.
